3. $hl - kl + hm - km - hn + kn =$

A. $(h + k)(l - m + n)$

B. $(h + k)(l + m - n)$

C. $(h - k)(l - m + n)$

D. $(h - k)(l + m - n)$
reasoning: To factor the expression $hl - kl + hm - km - hn + kn$, we group the terms with common factors: $(hl - kl) + (hm - km) - (hn - kn) = l(h - k) + m(h - k) - n(h - k)$. Now, we can factor out the common binomial $(h - k)$ from each term: $(h - k)(l + m - n)$. This matches option D.
